messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw repeated GPU saturation in us-west shared-pool this morning. One tenant (voicebot) ate ~70% of GPUs for ~30m and we hit 95th pct latency spikes across short jobs. Thinking we need a short-term "overdraft protection" + backlog window to avoid full soft-preemptions. :frowning_face:

maya: Can you paste the metrics? Was it sustained or noisy bursts? :thinking:

alex: Sustained with spikes. Snapshot: cpu_util=82%, gpu_util=87%, queue_depth(shared)=420, p95_latency=1.2s, p99=3.7s. The tenant had ~12 long-running streams + many short inferences.

sasha: Oof. Two quick ideas: 1) admission control with per-tenant queue caps + refill credits, 2) short penalty (priority drop) if tenant goes negative > window. Keeps them from starving others.

leo: For short-term, can we do an emergency soft-throttle on the offending tenant while we roll a better policy? Avoid evicting since paid dedicated customers exist.

jin: Important: any changes must respect reserved capacity and SLAs. How do tokens interact with dedicated tenants?

alex: Proposal: "tiered-credit" model. Reserved/premium tenants have a dedicated token pool (bypass up to reserved cap). Shared tenants use a refillable credit bucket. If a shared tenant drains below 0 for > overdraft_window we apply a progressive throttle and reduce queue slots. Also implement a global soft_headroom so the pool never goes >85% alloc.

maya: That sounds reasonable. Example config we could ship to admission-controller canary:```yaml
admission:
  per_tenant:
    queue_limit: 40            # max pending requests per tenant in shared pool
    refill_rate: 5             # credits per second
    overdraft_window: 120     # seconds allowed below zero before penalty
    penalty_decay: 3600       # seconds to fully recover priority
  global:
    soft_headroom_pct: 15      # keep 15% headroom for spikes
    enforce_on_burst: true
```

sasha: Love the config. We should also expose metrics: tenant_credits, tenant_overdraft_seconds, admission_dropped. I can add dashboards and alerts for >10 tenants with overdraft >30s.

leo: Worth considering model-fallback at admission time: if a tenant is over-consuming, allow older/smaller model variants transparently (with opt-out) so requests still succeed at lower cost. Cuts peak GPU time.

jin: +1 on explicit opt-out for customers. Also add a feature flag per-cluster so we can enable only for us-west canary.

alex: I'll draft a PR for the admission-controller plus the docs for the rollback plan. Plan: canary in us-west tomorrow AM, monitor p95/p99 and tenant_overdraft metrics for 2 hours. Sasha can own dashboards, Leo will coordinate model-fallback logic, Jin will sign-off on SLA checks.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: admission-controller-canary -> us-west at 2026-03-19T08:00Z (canary). Author: alex. :rocket:

maya: Thanks — ping me once canary is up, I'll run a synthetic noisy-tenant test to validate degradation behavior.

alex: Will do. If we see regressions we revert immediately. Goal is graceful queueing, not hard kills. :thumbsup:
